To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thermal degradation leads not only to reduction of dielectric strength but also to reduction of the ultimate strength and increased brittleness of the insulation material.

thermal degradation of insulation leads to degradation of the mechanical properties and this in turn leads to enhanced brittlement and formation of cracks in the insulation which in turn results in the formation of breakdown paths and eventual failure of insulation.

thermal degradation of insulation material leads to degradation of the mechanical properties and that this in turn leads to cracking of the insulation material and hence to a reduction of the breakdown strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an accelerated ageing model to predict the mechanical and dielectric properties of the insulation of low voltage high current electrical machines under accelerated ageing conditions.

the development of a methodology for testing the variation of mechanical properties of insulation materials as a function of thermal degradation and development of a model for the prediction of such degradation.
the study of the degradation of the mechanical properties of Polyimide insulation material as a function of temperature and time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mechanical properties of the insulation material play an important role in the breakdown of insulation and that the degradation of such properties should be considered as one of the key parameters in the insulation degradation process.
insulation degradation is a complex process and the occurrence of partial discharges is only a manifestation of this process.
the mechanical properties of the insulation play a vital role in the breakdown process of low voltage/high current insulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mechanical property degradation is an important aspect in the insulation ageing process and needs to be considered in the insulation life assessment process.
mechanical properties of insulation should be taken into account for the insulation degradation in HV motors.
thermal ageing of the insulation leads to degradation of its mechanical properties, which in turn may lead to cracking and subsequent breakdown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of class H insulation should be considered for the design and analysis of low voltage/high current electrical machines.
the thermal degradation of insulation leads to degradation of the mechanical properties of the insulation material.
thermal degradation of insulation in HV machines leads to reduction in ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of insulation material and the reduction in UTS is more pronounced at higher temperatures.
